narratives.narrative: The sense is 'rejoice with trembling' (101) and the type is affect (102): a felt movement of the interior, not an act performed. The bearer is the kings and rulers of the earth (105), summoned to serve. The operation (106) is the paradoxical joy of gladness held together with dread, and the target (107) is 'awed-joy' - the coupling (112) welds rejoice to trembling so neither cancels the other. Source is unmarked (103 present:false): no separate cause is named, the joy is simply the fitting response to the enthroned Son. No seat (104 'none') - not organ-located but a whole-self stance. No manner beyond the pairing (108 'none'); intensity, specifier, effect and prohibition are all unrecorded (109/110/111/113 present:false): the joy is not graded, not narrowed, not made a means to a further end, and never forbidden. The discovery (114) reads it as a submission that is glad yet never casual. Role is characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116) - the movement lives inside the person even as it faces the King.
narratives.story: Rulers are told to serve the Lord and, in the same breath, to rejoice while they tremble. This is not fear cancelling joy or joy cancelling fear; the two are fused into a single response - a gladness that never loses its awe. Nothing is said about what triggers it, how strong it is, or what it leads to; it is simply the right way for the powerful to stand before the enthroned King. It is a joy that keeps its reverence, felt deep in the person even as it looks upward.
narratives.variation_note: Uniquely among the eleven gil readings, this one welds joy to trembling (awed-joy) and gives it an unusual bearer - the kings and rulers of the earth summoned to submit - where every other gil reading grounds joy in salvation, trust, restoration, God's judgments, a festal day, or relation to God. Here the distinctive is the fusion of gladness with dread.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'joy greater than harvest' (101), an affect (102) placed in the heart. The bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is God having put more joy in the heart than the abundance of grain and wine gives, and the target (107) is 'surpassing-joy', coupled (112) as joy-over-harvest. Source is unmarked (103 present:false) at the row level, yet the operation makes God the giver - the joy is not self-generated but received. No seat (104 'none'): though the verse says 'heart', the reading treats the joy as a whole-self state. No manner (108); intensity, specifier, effect and prohibition are all absent (109/110/111/113 present:false) - the gladness is not measured, not qualified, not instrumental, not interdicted; it is terminal. The discovery (114) locates it in God and notes it outweighs the best material happiness. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalmist says God has put more joy in his heart than others feel at a bumper harvest of grain and wine. The gladness is a gift - God placed it there - and it simply outweighs the happiest material plenty. There is no measuring of how great it is or what it produces next; it stands on its own as an inner fullness. The point is stark: the best that abundance can give is surpassed by a joy that comes from God.
narratives.variation_note: This simchah reading places joy in the heart as a present possession outweighing material abundance, where #2 orients joy to its future destination (fullness in God's presence), #3 makes it the gladness filling the righteous' jubilation, #4 pictures it as seed sown for the upright, and #5 subordinates it beneath the memory of Jerusalem in exile. Here the distinctive is joy already given, surpassing plenty.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'rejoice in your salvation' (101), an affect (102). The bearer is the psalmist (105) at the gates of Zion; the operation (106) is the self recounting God's praises and rejoicing in his salvation, with target (107) 'salvation-joy', coupled (112) as rejoice-in-salvation. Source is unmarked (103 present:false) - no cause behind the salvation is named; the deliverance itself is the ground. No seat (104 'none'), a whole-self state; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect and prohibition are all absent (109/110/111/113 present:false): the joy is neither graded nor narrowed nor made a lever for something else nor forbidden. The discovery (114) notes the joy is grounded specifically in deliverance and voiced publicly at the daughter of Zion's gates. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: Standing at the gates of Zion, the psalmist gladly recounts God's praises and rejoices that he has been rescued. His joy is fixed on one thing - being saved - and it spills out openly, in a public place, for others to hear. Nothing is said about degrees of joy or where it leads; the deliverance itself is enough. Rescue becomes the reason to celebrate, and the celebration is not kept private.
narratives.variation_note: Same word (gil) and object as several readings - joy grounded in God's salvation - but here uniquely tied to a public setting (the gates of Zion) and welded to the recounting of praise, where #1 fuses it with trembling and #3 places it inside the heart after the act of trust.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'glad and exult in the Most High' (101), an affect (102). The bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the self being glad and exulting while singing praise to the name of the Most High, target (107) 'exultation', coupled (112) glad-and-exult. Source unmarked (103 present:false) - no separate trigger; the object itself, the Most High, draws the joy upward. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition all absent (109/110/111/113 present:false): the gladness is ungraded, unqualified, terminal, and never interdicted. The discovery (114) marks it distinct from the thanks-recital as an upward-leaping joy fixed on the Most High. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalmist declares he will be glad and exult in God, singing praise to the name of the Most High. This is joy reaching upward, fastened to God at his highest - not just thanking him for things, but delighting in who he is. The text does not measure the gladness or say what it produces; it simply lifts toward its greatest object. Gladness here is an upward leap of the whole person toward the Most High.
narratives.variation_note: One of twenty readings of samach ('glad'). Here the bearer is the singing psalmist and the joy leaps upward to 'the Most High', paired with exultation - distinct from the many communal or restoration-grounded gladness readings, and from the darker instances (Egypt's relief, the enemies' malice) where the same word carries no praise.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'heart rejoices in salvation' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the heart, having trusted, now rejoicing in God's salvation - joy following the decision to trust - with target (107) 'rejoicing', coupled (112) heart-rejoice. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the trust of the prior line is the pivot, but no cause is booked in this row. No seat (104 'none') though 'heart' is spoken - read as whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false): ungraded, unqualified, terminal, unforbidden. The discovery (114) distinguishes the joy from the trust itself: trust releases joy, and the once-sorrowing heart of v2 now rejoices. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: After the long lament of the psalm, the psalmist says his heart will rejoice in God's rescue. The joy comes on the far side of a decision to trust - trust opens the door and joy walks through it. The same heart that was full of sorrow now turns to gladness. Nothing is said about how strong the joy is or what it causes; it is simply the release that trust brings.
narratives.variation_note: This gil reading uniquely marks joy as the sequel to trust - the heart that first chose to rely on God then rejoices - where #1 fuses joy with trembling and #2 grounds it publicly at Zion's gates. The movement here is inward and sequential: sorrow, then trust, then joy.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'gladness of restoration' (101), an affect (102). The bearer is Jacob / Israel (105) - the joy is communal, not individual. The operation (106) is that when the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, Jacob rejoices and Israel is glad; the target (107) is 'restoration-joy', coupled (112) rejoice-at-restoring. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the restoring act is the ground, but no prior cause is named. No seat (104 'none'), whole-people state; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) sets this joy against the whole psalm's portrait of corruption: the interior reaches forward to a communal gladness for when God finally acts. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: At the very end of a psalm about human corruption, the hope breaks through: when God restores his people's fortunes, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad. This is a shared, forward-looking joy - not one person's feeling but a whole people longing for the day God acts. The gladness is still future, reached for across the darkness of the psalm. It is the community's answer to corruption: a joy held in hope of restoration.
narratives.variation_note: Unlike the individual gil readings (#1-#3), the bearer here is the whole people (Jacob/Israel) and the joy is anticipated, not present - reaching forward to God's restoring act. It is nearly identical to #8 (Psa 53:6), a doublet psalm; the difference is only its setting inside Psalm 14's portrait of universal corruption.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'fullness of joy in your presence' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is that in God's presence is fullness of joy and at his right hand pleasures forevermore - the anticipated end of the path of life - with target (107) 'anticipated-joy', coupled (112) fullness-of-joy. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the presence of God is the locus, not a named antecedent cause. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity is not booked as a graded value (109 present:false) even though 'fullness' implies completeness - the reading leaves it uncalibrated; specifier, effect, prohibition also absent (110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) notes the operation reaches to the destination: a joy made complete in God's own presence. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalmist looks down the path of life to its end and sees fullness of joy in God's presence, pleasures at his right hand that never run out. This is joy at its destination - not partial or passing but complete, found in being near to God. The text does not put a measure on it; it simply points to a gladness made whole in God's company. The hope of the whole psalm lands here: joy that is full because God is there.
narratives.variation_note: Where #1 grounds joy in the heart above harvest and #3-#4 fill present or communal rejoicing, this simchah reading is uniquely oriented to the future and the destination - joy 'made full' in God's presence at the end of the path of life.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'the heart gladdened by precepts' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the right precepts of the LORD rejoicing the heart - the word producing inner gladness - with target (107) 'gladdening', coupled (112) heart-rejoices. Source is unmarked as a row (103 present:false), yet the operation itself names the precepts as what gladdens - the cause is the word. No seat (104 'none') though 'heart' is named - read as whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition all absent (109/110/111/113 present:false): the gladness is ungraded, unqualified, terminal, unforbidden. The discovery (114) presses the point: the commandments do not merely bind, they gladden the interior that loves them. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalmist says God's right rules do something surprising - they make the heart glad. The law is not only a set of demands; to the one who loves it, it is a source of joy. What gladdens here is the word itself. The text does not weigh the joy or trace its effects; it simply reports that the precepts, being right, rejoice the heart.
narratives.variation_note: This samach ('rejoice') reading is unique among its group in that the joy is produced by God's word rather than by his saving acts, his presence, or a communal deliverance - the precepts themselves are what gladden the interior.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'rejoice over salvation' (101), an affect (102). The bearer is the people (105) - communal. The operation (106) is the people shouting for joy over the king's salvation and setting up banners in God's name; the target (107) is 'salvation-joy', coupled (112) shout-for-joy. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the king's deliverance is the occasion, no prior cause named. No seat (104 'none'), a whole-community state; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) reads it as the community's interior leaping in anticipated joy and marking the victory as God's. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The people say: may we shout for joy when the king is delivered, raising our banners in God's name. This is a shared, expectant joy - not yet fulfilled but leaned toward - and it credits the coming victory to God, not to the king. The gladness bursts out as a shout and a raised flag. The community's inner life reaches forward to celebrate a rescue it trusts God will give.
narratives.variation_note: This ranan/rua reading ('shout for joy') is communal and anticipatory - the people leaning toward the king's future deliverance - distinct from #2 (joy as the fitting act of the righteous), #3 (the redeemed soul's own shout), and #4 (the saints at God's dwelling).

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'exult in your strength' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the king (105); the operation (106) is the king rejoicing in God's strength and exulting greatly in his salvation - joy fixed on what God has done - target (107) 'exultation', coupled (112) exult-in-strength. Source unmarked (103 present:false): God's strength and salvation are the object, no separate antecedent booked. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity is not booked as a graded value (109 present:false) though the verse says 'how greatly' - the reading leaves the degree uncalibrated; specifier, effect, prohibition absent (110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) stresses the object: the joy rests on God's power and rescue, not the king's own prowess. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The king rejoices - and exults greatly - but not in himself. His joy is fastened to God's strength and God's rescue; the victory is God's doing. Even the exclamation 'how greatly he exults' is left unmeasured; the emphasis falls on where the joy is aimed, not how large it is. A powerful man's gladness is turned away from his own achievement and toward the God who saved him.
narratives.variation_note: Where most samach ('rejoice') readings have the people or the righteous as bearer, here the bearer is the king, and the joy is explicitly redirected off his own prowess onto God's strength and salvation - a deliberate refusal of self-congratulation.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'glad with the joy of your presence' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the king (105); the operation (106) is God making the king glad with the joy of his presence - gladness sourced in nearness to God - target (107) 'presence-gladness', coupled (112) glad-in-presence. Source unmarked as a row (103 present:false), yet the operation names God's presence (his face) as what makes glad. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false): ungraded, unqualified, terminal, unforbidden. The discovery (114) locates the deepest gladness in God's face itself, not merely in the gifts he gives. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116). Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: God makes the king glad - and the gladness comes from God's own presence, his face, not just from the blessings he hands out. The king has been given many good things, but the text reaches past the gifts to the giver: it is being near God that produces the deepest joy. Nothing is said about how strong the gladness is or what follows from it. The face of God is itself the source of the king's delight.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'my heart exults, I give thanks' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the helped heart exulting and, with song, the self giving thanks - joy overflowing into thanksgiving - target (107) 'exultant-thanks', coupled (112) heart-exults. Source unmarked as a row (103 present:false), but the received help is the pivot named in the discovery. No seat (104 'none') though 'heart' is spoken - whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) marks it distinct from trust: the help received turns the interior to leaping joy and song. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: Having been helped, the psalmist's heart leaps for joy and breaks into a song of thanks. The gladness does not stay silent inside; it spills over into praise. What sparks it is the help he received - trust gave way to rescue, and rescue turns the heart to exultant song. Joy here naturally becomes thanksgiving.
narratives.variation_note: This alats/exult reading has the psalmist's own heart as bearer and moves outward into thanksgiving-song, where #2 exults before God's revealed name, #3 (the wicked) exults in cruel triumph, and #4 carries exultation into the solitary night on one's bed.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'rejoice in the love that sees my soul' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the self rejoicing and being glad in God's steadfast love because he has seen its affliction and known the distress of its soul - joy that God knows the interior - target (107) 'being-known', coupled (112) rejoice-love-sees. Source unmarked as a row (103 present:false): God's steadfast love and his seeing are the ground, named in the operation not a separate source row. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) grounds the joy in being seen: the interior rejoices that its hidden distress is known to God. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalmist rejoices in God's steadfast love - and the reason is intimate: God has seen his affliction and known the distress of his soul. The joy is not that trouble is gone but that his hidden pain is fully known to God. To be seen and understood in one's deepest distress is itself the ground of gladness. Joy here is the relief of being known.
narratives.variation_note: Unlike the salvation- and presence-grounded gil readings, this one locates joy specifically in being seen and known by God in one's affliction - the object is God's noticing love, not a deliverance or a festal day.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'be glad and shout for joy, you upright' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the righteous / upright (105) - the call goes out to a community. The operation (106) is the self calling the righteous to be glad in the LORD, to rejoice and shout for joy, all the upright in heart - the confession ending in communal joy - target (107) 'summons-to-joy', coupled (112) glad-and-shout. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the forgiveness of the psalm is the occasion, not booked as a source row. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self/community; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) reads it as the close of the psalm: the relief of forgiveness becomes a summons for all the upright to rejoice. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalm of confession ends not in private relief but in a shout: be glad in the Lord, rejoice, all you upright in heart. One person's experience of forgiveness overflows into a call for the whole community to celebrate. Gladness becomes contagious, an invitation rather than a solitary feeling. The pardoned man cannot keep his joy to himself - he summons everyone who is upright to join it.
narratives.variation_note: This samach reading is a summons - the psalmist calling others into gladness at the end of a confession psalm - where other readings report the joy of a single bearer or a people already rejoicing. The distinctive move is joy turned into an invitation.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'shout for joy, you righteous' (101), an affect (102). Bearer is the righteous (105); the operation (106) is the self calling the righteous to shout for joy in the LORD, for praise befits the upright - joy as the fitting act of the righteous - target (107) 'fitting-joy', coupled (112) shout-for-joy. Source unmarked (103 present:false): no antecedent cause, the fittingness itself is the ground. No seat (104 'none'), whole-self; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) names joyful praise as the proper expression of an upright interior. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: The psalm opens with a command: shout for joy in the Lord, you righteous - because such praise suits the upright. Joy here is not just permitted but fitting, the natural and proper expression of a good and upright heart. It belongs to the righteous the way a voice belongs to a singer. The text presents joyful praise as simply what an upright person does.
narratives.variation_note: Where #1 is anticipatory (the people over a coming deliverance) and #3-#4 tie the shout to a redeemed soul or God's dwelling, this reading frames the joyful shout as intrinsically fitting to the righteous - joy as the proper act of an upright interior, with no particular deliverance in view.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'I told the glad news, I did not restrain my lips' (101). Uniquely in this family the type is volition (102), not affect - an act of the will, not merely a felt state. Bearer is the psalmist (105); the operation (106) is the self having told the glad news of deliverance in the great congregation and not restraining its lips - unrestrained public witness - target (107) 'unrestrained-witness', coupled (112) glad-news. Source unmarked (103 present:false): the deliverance is the content, no separate cause row. No seat (104 'none') though 'lips' are named in the verse - read as whole-self volition; no manner (108). Intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) reads it as a witness that refuses to hold back; the interior publishes God's rescue openly. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116). Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: The psalmist has told the good news of God's rescue to the whole assembly and deliberately refused to keep his lips shut. This is joy that becomes a decision - a chosen, willed act of witness, not just an inner feeling. He will not restrain himself; the rescue is too good to keep quiet. Gladness here drives a person to publish openly what God has done.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'glad shouts / ringing joy (rinnah)' (101), and the type is status (102) - a remembered condition rather than a present act. Bearer is the festal throng, remembered (105). Notably the operation (106) and target (107) are both booked 'none' (resolution none): there is no live movement, because the joy is only a memory - the reading refuses to invent a present operation. The coupling (112) is a genuine pair, welding the glad shouts to songs of thanksgiving (span to span). Source, intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition all absent (103/109/110/111/113 present:false); seat 'none' (104) and manner 'none' (108). The discovery (114) reads rinnah as the ringing gladness of the pilgrim throng, now only a painful memory. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116). Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: The psalmist, cast down and far from the temple, remembers how he once went with the crowd in glad shouts and songs of thanksgiving, keeping festival. The striking thing is that the joy is not happening now - it is only a memory, and a painful one. There is no present rejoicing to describe, just the ache of recalling it. The ringing gladness of worship survives here only as something lost and longed for.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'joy / rejoicing (gil - my exceeding joy)' (101), type status (102). Distinctively, the source IS marked here as a pair (103): the joy is led to by God's light and truth (v3), the two guides that bring him to the altar. Bearer is David (105); operation (106) is 'none' - the reading declines to fabricate a movement, holding the joy as a status. The target (107) is God himself. The coupling (112) pairs this joy with the exceeding gladness of the twin term. Seat 'none' (104), manner 'none' (108); intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) calls it the leaping joy that God is to David, reached when God's truth leads him to the altar. Role characteristic (115); and the locus is external:god (116) - the joy is seated in God, not merely in the self. Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: David calls God 'my exceeding joy' - God himself is the gladness he longs to reach at the altar. What leads him there is God's light and truth, sent out to guide him home. The joy is not a passing feeling he works up; it is fixed on God as its very object and resting place. Led by God's own truth, he comes to the altar to find his joy in God.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'joy / gladness (simchah - exceeding joy)' (101), type status (102). Bearer is David (105); the operation (106) is 'none' - held as a status, no invented movement. The target (107) is God ('my joy'), and uniquely the manner (108) is marked: 'exceeding / of my gladness' - God named as the very summit of gladness. The coupling (112) pairs it with the twin rejoicing (gil) of the same verse. Source, intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition all absent (103/109/110/111/113 present:false); seat 'none' (104). The discovery (114) reads God himself as 'the gladness of my joy' - the deepest delight is God at his altar, the goal of the light-led pilgrimage. Role characteristic (115); locus external:god (116). Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: David piles the words up: God is 'the gladness of my joy', his exceeding delight. He is not merely glad about something God gives; God himself is the height and summit of his gladness. The whole pilgrimage - led by God's light and truth - aims at this: to reach the altar and find that God is the deepest delight of all. Joy here is not about God; it is God.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'joy / gladness (simchah - with joy and gladness)' (101), type status (102). Bearer is the bridal procession (105) - the bride and her companions. The operation (106) and target (107) are 'none': the reading holds the gladness as the condition of the procession, not a discrete act. The manner (108) is marked: 'led to the king's palace' - the gladness accompanies the movement into the royal house. Source, intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (103/109/110/111/113 present:false); seat 'none' (104); coupling 'none' (112). The discovery (114) reads it as the festal joy of the wedding procession, the climax of the celebration. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116).
narratives.story: At the royal wedding, the bride and her companions are led into the king's palace with joy and gladness. The mood is festive, celebratory - the high point of the whole occasion. The gladness is simply the condition of the procession, the shared happiness of a wedding day as the party enters the palace. It is joy at its most public and communal, wrapped around a great celebration.
narratives.variation_note: This simchah 'gladness' reading is festal and communal - the wedding procession's shared joy - where #2 is the penitent's longed-for gladness, #3 the gladness that fills God's service, and #4 the gladness of God's redeemed nation. Here the joy attends a human celebration rather than being grounded in God's saving acts.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'gladness / joy (sason - oil of gladness)' (101), type status (102). Distinctively the source is marked as a pair (103): the gladness is conferred by God's anointing (v7) - God's act is its origin. Bearer is the king (105); operation (106) and target (107) are 'none' - held as a conferred status, not a movement performed. Seat 'none' (104), manner 'none' (108), coupling 'none' (112); intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (109/110/111/113 present:false). The discovery (114) reads the 'oil of gladness' as the joy conferred on the righteous-loving king, his joy surpassing his companions' - God's anointing being the qualifier. Role characteristic (115); locus internal:ib-state (116). Sole reading of this term - no cross-variation.
narratives.story: Because the king loves righteousness, God anoints him with the 'oil of gladness' above his companions. The joy is a gift poured out by God - conferred, not earned or worked up - and it lifts this king above his fellows. It comes with his anointing, marking him out. Gladness here is something God bestows on the one who loves what is right.

narratives.narrative: The sense is 'make glad / rejoice (samach)' (101), and here the type is action (102) - being made glad. Bearer is the king, made glad (105); the operation (106) is simply 'be made glad' - the king is the recipient, not the agent. The target (107) is 'none'. The manner (108) is marked: 'by stringed instruments' - festal music is the means. Source, intensity, specifier, effect, prohibition absent (103/109/110/111/113 present:false); seat 'none' (104); coupling 'none' (112). The gladness is a settled, secure peace at the very centre of chaos - because God is in her midst to help her. The raging waters cannot touch the calm joy of the place where God dwells. Here gladness is not excitement but steadiness: the deep contentment of being safe because God is present.

This is worship at its loudest and most exuberant - not one nation but all of them, clapping and shouting before God the King. The joy pours out physically, in noise and gesture, directed entirely at God. It is jubilation at full volume, the whole earth acclaiming its King.

Their rejoicing is twinned with the gladness of Zion, the whole community celebrating God's just rule. Here joy answers the sight of God setting things right.

Its gladness is bound together with the rejoicing of Judah's towns; city and villages celebrate as one. What lifts them is God's just judgment, the security of living under a King who rules rightly. The gladness he lost in guilt is the joy that belongs to being rescued, and he asks God to give it back and hold him up with a willing spirit. This is not a feeling he can manufacture; it flows from God's saving and must be restored by God. Joy here is the proper condition of the forgiven, prayed for after it was forfeited.

His guilt has felt like a crushing in his body, and he prays that gladness would reach down into that broken frame. Remarkably, the God who wounded him is the only one who can make his bones dance. The joy is that God's moral order holds and the innocent are vindicated.

Here, uniquely, joy is not celebrated but ranked - the exile swears to place the memory of Jerusalem above his greatest gladness. narratives.story: Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds. The joy does not stop when the worship service ends - it follows the faithful home, into the solitary hours of night, so that even lying on their beds they still exult and sing. Here joy is unbroken and private as well as public: the gladness of God's people spills past the assembly into the quiet of rest.
